children.translated_text: I bow devotedly to the guru, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the means of yoga,
who, like lord mercury, destroys old age and disease without remainder.
Having bowed to the pair of the guru's feet and having examined many tantras,
this compendium of rasa is made by <s>Śrī Gopālakṛṣṇa</s>.
Whatever perfected procedures there are, which are indeed accomplished through practice,

children.text: ekīkṛtya tu te sarve likhyante yatnato mayā ||
children.translated_text: all those are brought together and written down by me with care.
Because it is used in small quantity, because there is no distaste or unsuitable occasion,
and because it quickly gives health, <s>rasa</s> is superior to other medicines.
For curable diseases every medicine has been taught by knowers of reality;
but even in incurable diseases <s>rasa</s> should be given, and therefore it is called best.
When killed it kills old age and disease; when stupefied it destroys illness;
when bound it grants sky-going power. What other compassionate thing is there besides <s>sūta</s>?
<s>Rasendra</s>, <s>pārada</s>, <s>sūta</s>, <s>sūtarāja</s>, and <s>sūtaka</s>,

children.text: śivatejo rasaḥ sapta nāmānyevaṃ rasasya tu ||
children.translated_text: <s>śivatejas</s> and <s>rasa</s>: these are the seven names of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Śivabīja</s>, <s>rasa</s>, <s>sūta</s>, <s>pārada</s>, and <s>rasendraka</s>:
these are names of <s>rasa</s>, and there are others as stated in the Śiva tradition.
That which is deep blue within and bright without, shining like the midday sun,

children.text: śasto'tha dhūmraḥ paripāṇḍuraśca citro na yojyo rasakarmasiddhau ||
children.translated_text: is approved; but smoky, very pale, and variegated mercury should not be used for success in rasa operations.

children.text: nāgo vaṅgo malo vahniścāñcalyaṃ ca viṣaṃ giriḥ
children.translated_text: Lead, tin, impurity, fire, mobility, poison, and mountain,
and intolerance of fire: these great faults are naturally present in mercury.

children.text: vraṇaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ tathā jāḍyaṃ dāhaṃ vīryasya nāśanam
children.translated_text: Wound, skin disease, dullness, burning, loss of virility,
death, inertness, and eruptions: these produce these effects in men respectively.
Therefore the best among physicians should perform the purification of <s>rasa</s>.
When purified, this <s>rasa</s> is nectar itself; when joined with faults, it is poison.
When <s>sūta</s> is free of faults, then it removes death and fever.
When purified, this <s>rasa</s> is nectar itself; when joined with faults, it is poison.
Now then I shall fully explain the purification of mercury.
The <s>rasa</s> should be taken under an auspicious constellation, in a quantity of one hundred palas.
Or fifty, twenty-five, ten, five, or even one may be taken;
an excellent processing of <s>rasa</s> should not be done with less than a pala.
A hundred, five hundred, twenty-five, or ten,

children.text: pañcaikaṃ vā palaṃ caiva palārddhaṃ karṣameva ca ||
children.translated_text: or five, one pala, half a pala, or one karṣa may also be used.
An excellent processing of <s>rasa</s> should not be done with less than a karṣa.
In all practical applications one should arrange it according to what is available.
On an auspicious day, having meditated on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, one should properly worship <s>Kumārī</s> and the young initiate.
In this firm mortar, produced from good iron or stone and having a cavity four fingers deep,
after preparing protection joined with his own mantra in the well-heated mortar, with steady and sound understanding,
one who knows it, undistracted in mind and joined with devotion to <s>Śiva</s>, should perform the operation of <s>rasa</s>.
To the non-terrible, to the terrible, and to those more terrible than the terrible,
to all, O <s>Śarva</s>, to every form of <s>Śarva</s>, homage to you, to the forms of <s>Rudra</s>.
One should put goat dung, husk, and fire, the three, into an underground pit.
The mortar placed above it is known as a heated mortar.
The milks produced from <s>snuhī</s> and <s>arka</s>, <s>brahmabīja</s>, guggulu,
and twice as much rock salt are to be ground; this is a most excellent fetter.
The physician should grind the <s>rasa</s> together with powders in sixteenth parts,
adding each one on each day, and should grind it thoroughly seven times.
Ground for a day with <s>sorṇa</s>, niśeṣṭakā, smoke, and citron-water,
and washed with sour gruel, the <s>rasa</s> gives up the fault of lead.
With powder of <s>viśālā</s> and <s>aṅkoṭha</s> it releases the fault of tin.
<s>Rājavṛkṣa</s> removes impurity, and <s>citraka</s> removes the fire-defect.
Black <s>dhustūra</s> removes mobility; <s>triphala</s> destroys poison.
The three pungents remove the mountain fault, and <s>trikaṇṭaka</s> removes intolerance of fire.
For each fault, the corresponding powder, in a sixteenth part, together with <s>kanyaka</s>,
should be taken up, and the wise man should wash it in an earthen vessel with hot sour gruel.
Thus purified, <s>sūta</s> is freed from the seven coverings.
With liquids of sandalwood, devakāṣṭha, kākajaṅghā, and jayā,
and after adding liquids of cucumber, mūsalī, and kanyā, one should grind it.
After one day one should distill it; then one should use it as purified.
One should grind <s>sūta</s> for a day with <s>kumārī</s> and powders of turmeric.
One should distill it in a distillation apparatus; the <s>rasa</s> becomes properly purified.
Adding sulphur in one-twelfth part of the <s>rasa</s>, one should grind it.
It is to be cooked for a watch in a distillation apparatus with liquids arising from citron.
It should be ground again and cooked again seven times for purification.
With the juice of <s>jayantī</s>, of <s>vardhamāna</s>, and of fresh ginger,
and likewise in sequence with that of <s>vāyasī</s>, this grinding is the purification of <s>rasa</s>.
The discerning man should grind it separately with the fresh juice of each of these
until it becomes dry, seven times.
Having taken it up, the wise man should wash it in an earthen pot with hot sour gruel.
Completely freed from all faults and rid of the seven coverings,
this becomes purified <s>sūta</s> and is fit for all operations.
Ground with niśeṣṭakā, smoke-dust, and acid, it becomes without covering, and then with <s>sorṇa</s>;
<s>sūta</s> is ground with excellent sour gruel, fire, <s>kanyaka</s>, and the three pungents.
One should grind <s>sūta</s> for one day with liquids produced from <s>kumārī</s>.
Likewise, one should triturate it for one day with decoctions made from <s>citraka</s>.
Together with the juices of <s>kākamācī</s>, one should triturate it for one day.
Mercury should be triturated carefully with the fresh juices of garlic and those arising from betel leaves,
and likewise with a decoction of <s>triphalā</s>.
Then, separating the mercury from these substances and washing it with sour gruel,
one should employ it in mercurial operations when it is freed from all defects.
One should triturate three parts of mercury with one part of <s>arka</s>,
using lemon juice until it reaches the condition of a lump.
That lump is placed in a lower vessel, and water is put in the upper vessel.
Having made even a channel or basin, one should then collect the mercury.
This is called upward distillation by physicians in the purification of mercury.
Having rubbed sulfur, called butter-like, for a day with lemon water,
with <s>vānarī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, and <s>śikhi</s>, mixed with rock-salt and mustard,
one should make the mercury into a destroyed paste and smear it on the upper vessel.
Having smeared the belly of the upper vessel, the lower vessel should be supplied with water.

children.text: sandhilepaṃ dvayoḥ kṛtvā tad yantraṃ bhuvi pūrayet
children.translated_text: Having sealed the junction of the two, one should bury that apparatus in the ground.

children.text: upariṣṭāt puṭe datte jale patati pāradaḥ
children.translated_text: When a heating pit is applied above, the mercury falls into the water.
This is called downward distillation by accomplished masters and others in mercurial work.

children.text: ghaṭe rasaṃ vinikṣipya sajalaṃ ghaṭam anyakam
children.translated_text: Putting mercury in a pot, and making another pot containing water

children.text: tiryaṅmukhaṃ dvayoḥ kṛtvā tanmukhaṃ rodhayet sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the mouths of the two turned sideways, the wise man should close their opening.
He should kindle fire below the mercury until the mercury enters the water.
This is called lateral distillation by adepts such as <s>Nāgārjuna</s>.
Mercury, when thus badly treated, acquires impotence.

children.text: tanmuktaye'sya kriyate bodhanaṃ kathyate hi tat ||
children.translated_text: For freeing it from that, awakening is performed; that is now described.
Either in a <s>Viśvāmitra</s> skull, or else in a glass bottle,
one should pour water upon the mercury there, enough for it to be immersed.
One should fill it and keep it in the ground for three days to the measure of an elephant's trunk.
By this, this king of mercury gives up its impotent condition.
Or mercury should be obtained from cinnabar; that is stated as follows.
Cinnabar, triturated for a day with the water of lemon and neem,
should be collected by means of an upward-distillation apparatus as pure mercury.
Freed from coverings such as lead and tin, it is fit for mercurial operations.
This mercury accomplishes all operations even without the set of eight processes.
Steaming and trituration, likewise swooning and raising,
distillation and awakening, and after that regulation,
and kindling: these are proclaimed as the eight preparations of mercury.
Having made cinnabar as coarse as rice grains, in an earthen vessel for three days
it should repeatedly be impregnated with lemon juices or with the juices of <s>cāṅgerī</s>.
Then, having drenched it with lemon water and the juice of <s>cāṅgerī</s>,
placing it in the middle of a cooking pot, and above it a well-rubbed hard lid,

children.text: uttānaṃ cāruśarāvaṃ tatra triṃśadvāraṃ jalaṃ deyam
children.translated_text: one should set an overturned, handsome earthen saucer there and pour in water thirty times.

children.text: uṣṇaṃ heyaṃ tathaiva tadūrdhvapātanena nirmmalaḥ śivajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The hot water should be discarded likewise; by that upward distillation the mercury born of <s>Śiva</s> becomes pure.
Cinnabar should be ground with the juices of <s>pāribhadra</s> for the measure of one watch,
or else with the juices of lemons, and cooked in a distillation apparatus.
That mercury, free from the seven coverings, should be used in a compound.
Even without further purification, this is pure in mercurial operations.

children.text: gandhakena rasaṃ prājñaḥ sudṛḍhaṃ mardayed bhiṣak
children.translated_text: A learned physician should triturate mercury very firmly with sulfur.
When the mercury has the appearance of collyrium, having abandoned its dense mobility,
then it should be known by experts in mercury as swooned.
According to the use of its accompanying vehicle, it destroys masses of diseases.
Two palas of purified mercury and half as much sulfur as mercury
should be triturated continuously for one day with the juice of <s>kanyā</s>.
Having sealed it, one should kill it in a heating pit for one day in the <s>bhūdhara</s> apparatus.
One should thoroughly triturate mercury with the juice of <s>bhujaṅgavallī</s>.
Placed in a sealed crucible made from the root-tuber of <s>karkaṭī</s>, it should be heated in a gentle fire.
That ash becomes a carrier of efficacy and should be used in all operations.
Mercury should be triturated for three days with the juices of the roots of white <s>aṅkoṭha</s>.
One should heat it in a blind crucible, and the mercury attains the state of ash.
<s>Devadālī</s>, <s>haṃsapadī</s>, <s>yamaciñcā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>:
with these, mercury should be rubbed; from heating, it surely dies.

children.text: bhāgo rasasya traya eva bhāgā gandhasya māṣaḥ pavanāśanasya
children.translated_text: One part of mercury, three parts of sulfur, and one māṣa of <s>pavanāśana</s>

children.text: saṃmardya gāḍhaṃ sakalaṃ subhāṇḍe tāṃ kajjalīṃ kācaghaṭe nidadhyāt ||
children.translated_text: should all be triturated firmly in a good vessel, and that black sulfide paste should be placed in a glass pot.

children.text: saṃrudhya mṛtkarpaṭakair ghaṭīṃ tāṃ mukhe sucūrṇāṃ khaṭikāṃ ca dattvā
children.translated_text: Having sealed that pot with clay-smeared cloths and placed well-powdered chalk at its mouth,

children.text: kramāgninā trīṇi dināni paktvā tāṃ vālukāyantragatāṃ tataḥ syāt ||
children.translated_text: one should cook it with gradually increasing fire for three days, after it has been set in a sand apparatus.
The ash of the lord-born mercury, red like the flower of <s>bandhūka</s>, should be employed in all diseases.

children.text: nijānupānair maraṇaṃ jarāṃ ca hantyasya vallaḥ kramasevanena ||
children.translated_text: With its own vehicles, and by gradual use, a dose of it destroys death and old age.

children.text: palamātraṃ rasaṃ śuddhaṃ tāvanmātraṃ tu gandhakam
children.translated_text: One pala of purified mercury and just the same measure of sulfur
should be made into kajjalī according to rule, with water from banyan sprouts.
Having given three impregnations, one should place it in the middle of a cooking pot.
Having constructed a jacket-apparatus, one should fill it with sand.
Then the physician should apply a gentle fire for four watches.
Rasasindūra is produced, resembling the young sun.
According to the particular accompanying vehicle, it produces various virtues.

children.text: pṛthak samaṃ samaṃ kṛtvā pāradaṃ gandhakaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having made the <s>pārada</s> (mercury) and likewise the sulfur separately in equal portions,
with <s>narasāra</s>, <s>dhūmasāra</s>, and <s>sphaṭika</s>, each for the measure of a watch,
one should triturate them with lemon juice and place them in a glass bottle.
Having put stone-chalk at the mouth, one should smear on a sealing clay.
One should wrap it separately with seven layers of clay-smeared cloth, drying each one.

children.text: sacchidrāyāṃ mṛdaḥ sthālyāṃ kupikāṃ tāṃ niveśayet ||
children.translated_text: One should place that bottle in an earthen pot furnished with holes.

children.text: pūrayet sikatāpūrair ā galaṃ matimān bhiṣak
children.translated_text: The wise physician should fill it with a heap of sand up to the neck.

children.text: niveśya cullyāṃ dahanaṃ mandaṃ madhyaṃ kharaṃ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Having set it on the stove, he should kindle the fire successively as mild, medium, and fierce.
After heating through twelve watches, he should take it out when it has cooled of itself.
Having broken it open, he should discard the pearl-like mass adhering above.
The <s>rasasindūra</s> situated below should be used in all diseases.

children.text: ṭaṅkaṇaṃ madhu lākṣā ca ūrṇāguñjāyuto rasaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, honey, <s>lākṣā</s>, and mercury joined with wool and <s>guñjā</s>,
when triturated with the juices born from <s>bhṛṅga</s> for one day, should again be stirred.
When blown in the fire, it becomes an ash resembling pure camphor.

children.text: piṣṭaṃ pāṃśupaṭupragāḍham amalaṃ vajryambunā naikaśaḥ sūtaṃ dhātugataṃ khaṭīkavalitaṃ taṃ sampuṭe rodhayet
children.translated_text: Mercury that has entered metal, ground many times with clean, strong earth and salt and with diamond-water, and enclosed with chalk, should be confined in a sealed capsule.

children.text: antaḥsthaṃ lavaṇasya tasya ca tale prajvālya vahniṃ dṛḍhaṃ ghasraṃ grāhyamathendukundadhavalaṃ bhasmoparisthaṃ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Placed inside salt, and with a strong fire kindled beneath it, after a day the ash lying above, white as the moon and jasmine, should then be gently collected.

children.text: tadvalladvitayaṃ lavaṅgasahitaṃ prātaḥ prabhuktaṃ nṛṇām ūrdhvaṃ recayati dviyāmamasakṛtpeyaṃ jalaṃśītalam
children.translated_text: Two <s>ratti</s>s of that, together with clove, when eaten by men in the morning, purges upward for two watches; cold water should be drunk repeatedly.

children.text: etaddhanti ca vatsarādhikaviṣaṃ ṣāṇmāsikaṃ māsikaṃ śailotthaṃ garalaṃ mṛgendrakuṭilodbhūtaṃ ca tātkālikam ||
children.translated_text: This destroys poison more than a year old, six-month-old poison, monthly poison, mineral poison, venom arisen from a lion or a crooked creature, and immediate poison.
One should firmly triturate mercury and sulfur with the juices of <s>hastiśuṇḍī</s>,
or else with the juices of <s>bhūdhātrikā</s>, up to the end of seventy days.
Having rubbed it in a sand apparatus, one should place it in a crucible.
For one day, until night, one should heat it in the fire very gently.

children.text: evaṃ niṣpādyate pītaḥ śītaḥ sūtastu gṛhyate
children.translated_text: Thus yellow mercury is produced; when cool, the mercury is collected.
One should continually eat a beneficial <s>guñjā</s>-measure of it with a complete piece.
It first produces awareness of hunger and destroys abdominal diseases.
It is excellent for destroying old age, and likewise gives prosperity and happiness.
It generates enthusiasm in the heart and grants handsome sons.
It always gives strength in the body and is intent on destroying old age.
It destroys in an instant every disorder such as breaking pain in the limbs.
There is no mercury preparation higher than this, the beautiful-in-all-limbs <s>rasa</s>.
One should kill equal parts of grain-processed mica and mercury with killing liquids.

children.text: dinaikaṃ tena kalkena vastraṃ liptvā tu varttikām ||
children.translated_text: For one day, having smeared cloth with that paste, one should make a wick.

children.text: vilipya tailairvartiṃ tām eraṇḍotthaiḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having repeatedly anointed that wick with oils produced from castor,
one should light it in a vessel of ghee and collect whatever has fallen.
That becomes black ash, and it should again be triturated with regulating substances.
For one day one should make it fall in the apparatus called <s>kaṇṭuka</s>; there is no doubt.
That becomes killed mercury, and it should be applied in the respective diseases.

children.text: śvetaṃ pītaṃ raktaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ ceti caturvidham
children.translated_text: White, yellow, red, and black: these are the four kinds.
Among the characteristics of mercury ashes, each succeeding one is superior.
Two parts of burnt husk and one part of anthill clay,
one part of iron slag and a part of white stone,
with a little equal to human hair, should be ground with goat's milk.

children.text: yāmamātraṃ dṛḍhaṃ mardyaṃ tena mūṣāṃ prakalpayet ||
children.translated_text: It should be firmly triturated for the measure of a watch; with that one should fashion a crucible.
Having dried it, placed mercury inside, and sealed it with those pastes,
this is called a diamond crucible, effective for properly preparing mercury.
<s>Sarpākṣī</s>, wild <s>karkoṭī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, and <s>yamaciñcikā</s>,
<s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>śaṅkhapuṣpī</s>, <s>śarapuṅkhā</s>, and <s>punarnavā</s>,
<s>maṇḍūkaparṇī</s>, <s>matsyākṣī</s>, <s>brahmadaṇḍī</s>, and <s>śikhaṇḍinī</s>,

children.text: anantā kākajaṅghā ca kākamācī ca potikā ||
children.translated_text: <s>anantā</s>, <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>kākamācī</s>, and <s>potikā</s>,
<s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>sahacarā</s>, <s>sahadevī</s>, and <s>mahābalā</s>,
<s>balā</s>, <s>nāgabalā</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, and the two <s>cakramarda</s> and <s>karañja</s>,
<s>pāṭhā</s>, <s>tāmalakā</s>, <s>nīlī</s>, <s>jālinī</s>, and <s>padmacāriṇī</s>,
<s>ghaṇṭā</s>, <s>vighaṇṭā</s>, <s>gojihvā</s>, <s>kokilākṣa</s>, and <s>ghanadhvani</s>,
<s>ākhukarṇī</s>, <s>kṣīriṇī</s>, <s>tripuṭī</s>, and <s>meṣaśṛṅgikā</s>,

children.text: kṛṣṇavarṇā ca tulasī siṃhī ca girikarṇikā
children.translated_text: black-colored <s>tulasī</s>, <s>siṃhī</s>, and <s>girikarṇikā</s>:
these are the regulating herbs, furnished with flowers, roots, and leaves.
<s>Ghana</s>, <s>vacā</s>, <s>citraka</s>, <s>gokṣura</s>, <s>kaṭutumbī</s>, <s>dantikā</s>, and <s>jātī</s>,
<s>sarpākṣī</s>, <s>śarapuṅkhā</s>, <s>kanyā</s>, and the bulb of <s>cāṇḍālinī</s>,

children.text: viṣamuṣṭivajravallyau lajjā lākṣā ca devadālī ca
children.translated_text: <s>viṣamuṣṭi</s> and <s>vajravallī</s>, <s>lajjā</s>, <s>lākṣā</s>, and <s>devadālī</s>,
<s>sahadevī</s>, <s>nīpakaṇā</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and the two <s>cakra</s> and <s>lāṅgalikā</s>,
<s>māṇārka</s>, <s>candrarekhā</s>, <s>ravibhaktā</s>, <s>kākamācikā</s>, and <s>arka</s>,

children.text: viṣṇukrāntā vāyasatuṇḍī vajrī balā ca śuṇḍī ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>viṣṇukrāntā</s>, <s>vāyasatuṇḍī</s>, <s>vajrī</s>, <s>balā</s>, and <s>śuṇḍī</s>,
<s>koṣātakī</s>, <s>jayantī</s>, <s>vārāhī</s>, <s>hastiśuṇḍikā</s>, and <s>rambhā</s>,
<s>matsyākṣī</s>, <s>yamaciñcā</s>, the two <s>haridrā</s>s, and the two <s>punarnavā</s>s,

children.text: dhustūrakākajaṅghe śatāvarī kañcukī ca vandhyā ca
children.translated_text: <s>dhustūra</s>, <s>kākajaṅghā</s>, <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>kañcukī</s>, and <s>vandhyā</s>,
<s>tilabhekaparṇī</s>, <s>dūrvā</s>, <s>mūrvā</s>, <s>harītakī</s>, and <s>tulasī</s>,
<s>gokaṇṭaka</s> and <s>ākhuparṇī</s>, <s>karkaṭīkanda</s>, <s>vargalatā</s>,
<s>musalī</s>, <s>hiṅgu</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>śigru</s>, <s>girikarṇikā</s>, and <s>mahārāṣṭrī</s>,
<s>mārkava</s>, <s>saindhava</s>, <s>saraṇī</s>, <s>somalatā</s>, white mustard, and <s>asanaka</s>,
<s>haṃsapadī</s>, <s>vyāghrapādī</s>, <s>kiṃśuka</s>, <s>bhallātaka</s>, and <s>indravāruṇikā</s>.

children.text: sarvaṃ cārddhāṃśaṃ vā aṣṭādaśādhikaṃ vāpi dravyam
children.translated_text: All the substance, or half of it, or even an amount increased by eighteen parts,
is to be used according to rule by those who know the proper method in killing and stupefying mercury and similar operations.
Sour vetasa, citron, luṅga, the sour juice of chickpeas,

children.text: nāgaraṅgaṃ tintiḍī ca ciñcāpatraṃ ca nimbukam ||
children.translated_text: nāgaraṅga, tamarind, leaves of tamarind, and lemon,

children.text: cāṅgerī dāḍimaṃ caiva karamardaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: cāṅgerī, pomegranate, and likewise karamarda:
this is declared to be the group of sour substances, together with sour vetasa.

children.text: lavaṇāni ca kathyante sāmudraṃ saindhavaṃ viḍam
children.translated_text: Now the salts are stated: sea-salt, rock-salt, viḍa salt,
sauvarcala, romaka, and also cullikā salt.
The urines of elephant, camel, buffalo, donkey, and horse,
and of cow, goat, and sheep, of women and of men, are declared to be the group of urines.
Guñjā, borax, honey, ghee, and jaggery are the five liquefying agents.
Bile is fivefold, born from fish, cow, horse, antelope, and peacock.
Svarjikā, borax, and yavakṣāra are declared to be alkalis.

children.text: prātareva purato virecanaṃ taddinopavasanaṃ vidhāya ca
children.translated_text: In the morning, having first performed purgation and having fasted on that day,
on the next day one should take wholesome food, and on the following day one should consume <s>rasendra</s> (processed mercury).
Intellect, memory, radiance, beauty, strength, and also rasa itself
all these increase for people under the regimen of consuming rasa.

children.text: hitaṃ mudgāmbu dugdhājyaṃ śālyannaṃ ca viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Beneficial are mung-bean water, milk, ghee, and especially rice food,

children.text: śākaṃ paunarnavaṃ vāstu meghanādaṃ ca yūthikām ||
children.translated_text: greens such as punarnavā, vāstu, meghanāda, and yūthikā.
One should eat salt, māgadhī, musta, and lotus roots;

children.text: anupānaṃ tu dātavyaṃ jñātvā rogādikaṃ bhiṣak ||
children.translated_text: but the physician should give the accompanying drink after determining the disease and other factors.
Pumpkin, cucumber, watermelon, bitter gourd,
kusumbhikā, karkoṭī, kalambī, and kākamācikā:
this set of eight beginning with ka should be avoided by one who eats rasa.
Sulphur, diamond, vaikrānta, diamond-mica, orpiment, realgar,
kharpara, śikhituṇḍa, vimala, and gold pyrite,
green vitriol, lodestone, cowries, collyrium, cinnabar,
red ochre, conch, earth-worm, borax, and bitumen:

children.text: ete coparasāḥ proktāḥ śodhyā māryā vidhānataḥ ||
children.translated_text: these are declared to be the secondary minerals; they must be purified and killed according to rule.

children.text: śvetadvīpe purā devyāḥ krīḍantyāḥ prasṛtaṃ rajaḥ
children.translated_text: Long ago, in Śvetadvīpa, while the Goddess was sporting, her menstrual blood flowed forth;
when she had bathed in the ocean of milk, her garment, stained with that blood,
was washed in those waters; in that place sulphur, fragrant by nature, is remembered as having arisen.

children.text: caturdhā gandhakaḥ prokto raktaḥ pītaḥ sito'sitaḥ
children.translated_text: Sulphur is said to be fourfold: red, yellow, white, and black.
The red is praised for operations with gold; the yellow and white are for rejuvenation;
the white is for application on wounds and the like; the black is the best and very rare.

children.text: aśuddhagandhaḥ kurute tu tāpaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ bhramaṃ pittarujāṃ karoti
children.translated_text: Impure sulphur produces heat, skin disease, dizziness, and disorders of bile;

children.text: rūpaṃ balaṃ vīryasukhaṃ nihanti tasmātsuśuddho viniyojanīyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: it destroys beauty, strength, virility, and happiness. Therefore only well-purified sulphur should be employed.
Sulphur is called gandhapāṣāṇa, śukapuccha, sugandhaka,
saugandhika, enemy of copper, enemy of scabies, and navanītaka.

children.text: sājyaṃ bhāṇḍe payaḥ kṣiptvā mukhaṃ vastreṇa bandhayet
children.translated_text: Having poured milk together with ghee into a vessel, one should bind its mouth with cloth;
having placed sulphur on its back, one should cover it with a shallow dish.

children.text: bhāṇḍaṃ nikṣipya bhūmyantarūrdhve deyaṃ puṭaṃ laghu
children.translated_text: After setting the vessel in the ground, one should give a light heating from above;

children.text: tataḥ kṣīre drutaṃ gandhaṃ śuddhaṃ yogeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: then the sulphur melted into the milk should be used, purified, in preparations.
Putting ghee in an iron vessel, one should heat it over the fire;
when the ghee is hot, one should add to it an equal amount of sulphur powder.
Seeing that the sulphur has melted, one should cast it into milk;
thus the purification of sulphur is accomplished, and it may be used in all diseases.
Purified sulphur removes diseases, including skin disease, death-threatening illness, and fever;
it kindles the digestive fire, is very hot, and increases virility.

children.text: gaṃdhaścātirasāyanaḥ sumadhuraḥ pāke kaṭūṣṇānvitaḥ kaṇḍūkuṣṭhavisarpadarpadalano dīptānalaḥ pācanaḥ
children.translated_text: Sulphur is a supreme rejuvenative, sweet, pungent and hot in digestion, destroying the pride of itching, skin disease, and erysipelas, kindling the fire and promoting digestion;

children.text: āmonmanthanaśodhano viṣaharaḥ sūtācca vīryapradaḥ gaurīpuṣpabhavas tathā krimiharaḥ svarṇādhikaṃ vīryyakṛt ||
children.translated_text: it churns and purifies undigested matter, counteracts poison, gives potency beyond mercury, is born from the flower of <s>Gaurī</s>, destroys worms, and produces power greater than gold.
Pain in the side, anemia, nausea, a continuous burning sensation,
a mass of diseases, and heaviness are caused by unpurified diamond.
Diamond placed inside vyāghrī tuber and cooked in a swing apparatus
for seven days in decoction of kodrava or kulattha becomes stainless.
Diamond placed inside vyāghrī tuber should be cooked in a swing apparatus;
after removing it after a day and night, one should sprinkle it with horse urine,
or sprinkle the thunderbolt-stone with the milk of vajrī; it becomes stainless.
Taking the root of a cotton plant that is three years old, one should grind it;
one should further grind it with the own juices of the threefold group and of betel leaf.
One should place the diamond inside that pellet, seal it, and cook it in a gajapuṭa heating;
in this way, by seven puṭas, the thunderbolt-stone is certainly killed.

children.text: kāṃsyapātre tu bhekasya mūtre vajraṃ tu nikṣipet
children.translated_text: One should place diamond in a bronze vessel in the urine of a frog;
heated twenty-one times, the diamond thus becomes killed.
Heated twenty-one times, one should sprinkle it with donkey urine;
having pounded orpiment with hammers, one should place the thunderbolt-stone in that pellet.
Blown in the fire and sprinkled with horse urine according to the previous procedure,
that diamond becomes ash and makes the body adamantine.
Diamond ash is long-life-giving, productive of happiness, and bestows strength and beauty;
it destroys disease and removes death in full measure.
Vaikrānta should be purified like diamond and blown in horse urine.
That ash, called hima, should be combined by the skilled in place of diamond.

children.text: vaikrāntaṃ vajravacchodhyaṃ māraṇaṃ caiva tasya tat
children.translated_text: <s>Vaikrānta</s> should be purified like diamond, and its killing is the same as that.
It should be sprinkled with horse urine and heated again and again twenty-one times.
Then the five parts of northern <s>vāruṇī</s> should be placed into a ball.

children.text: ruddhvā mūṣāpuṭe pācyaṃ uddhṛtya golake punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having sealed it, it should be cooked in a crucible-heating; after taking it out, again in a ball,
having placed it and sealed it, one should cook it in this way until it reaches the state of ash.
When <s>vaikrānta</s> has become ash, it should be used in place of diamond.
<s>Abhraka</s> is the seed of the mountain-born goddess, spotless, and called gaganā.

children.text: tatra kṛṣṇābhrake vajraṃ pītātmani tu grāhikam
children.translated_text: Among these, in black <s>abhraka</s> there is vajra; in the yellow kind there is grāhika.
In the white kind there is tāraka, and in the red kind the excellent bhīruka.
That which is very excellent, hard-bodied, heavy, and resembling collyrium,

children.text: yanna śabdāyate vahnau naivocchūnaṃ bhaved api
children.translated_text: which does not make a sound in fire and does not become swollen either,
born from a good mine, is famed as dense vajra-abhraka.

children.text: pinākaṃ darduraṃ nāgaṃ vajraṃ ceti caturvidham
children.translated_text: It is fourfold: pināka, dardura, nāga, and vajra.
When smelted, pināka-abhraka readily gives off a mass of flakes.
The nāga makes a hissing sound; the dardura sounds like a frog.

children.text: caturthaṃ ca varaṃ jñeyaṃ na vahnau vikṛtiṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: The fourth should be known as the best, for it undergoes no alteration in fire.
Pināka causes skin disease; dardura causes death.

children.text: nāgaṃ dehagataṃ nityaṃ vyādhiṃ kuryād bhagandaram ||
children.translated_text: Nāga, when present in the body, continually produces the disease fistula-in-ano.

children.text: rase rasāyane caiva yojyaṃ vajrābhrakaṃ priye
children.translated_text: In mercury work and in rasāyana, dear one, vajra-abhraka should be employed.
Therefore vajra-abhraka should be taken, for it conquers disease, old age, and death.
Impure abhraka destroys life and increases vāta and kapha.
Unstruck, it cuts the body and increases weak digestion and worms.
Abhraka mixed with one quarter part of rice should be put inside a blanket.
One should keep it in water for three nights; when it is soaked, one should rub it firmly.
That which has fallen through the blanket, is smooth, and free from sand,
is called dhānyābhraka, for the successful killing of abhraka.
Sprinkled with decoction of triphalā, cow urine, milk, and sour gruel,

children.text: bhastrāgnau saptadhā vyoma taptaṃ taptaṃ viśudhyati ||
children.translated_text: vyoma, heated again and again seven times in a bellows-fire, becomes purified.
Or one should throw smelted abhraka into a decoction of jujube.
Rubbed by hand and dried, it surpasses dhānyābhraka.
Ground with water of <s>Agastya</s> flowers, together with elephant-foot yam tuber,
and kept for a month in cattle-shed earth, it becomes like mercury.
Having taken vajra-abhraka and placed it inside a cooking vessel,
one should cook it with plantain and other alkaline water, by a fire of cow dung.
Until it becomes like vermilion on the outside of the vessel,
it should then be sprinkled with milks, and afterwards finely powdered.
Having taken dhānyābhraka, one should give three puṭa-heatings with decoctions of mustā.
In the same way, separately with waters of punarnavā and likewise with juices of kāsamarda,
with juices of nāgavallī and with the milks of saryya, each separately it should be given.
After rubbing it day by day with decoctions produced from banyan roots,
having then given three puṭas, one should heat it three times with waters of musalī,
three times with a decoction of gokṣura, and three times with juices of vānarī.
It should be cooked with juices of plantain tuber, and for three nights with kokilākṣa plants.
One should heat it with juices of lodhra, and again give one puṭa with milk.

children.text: dadhnā ghṛtena madhunā svacchayā sitayā tathā
children.translated_text: With curd, ghee, honey, clear water, and sugar as well,
one should give one puṭa with each; in this way the death of abhraka is accomplished.
Vyoma then becomes a remover of all diseases and a yogavāhin, a carrier of efficacy.
It destroys the intoxication and pride of women and is recommended for those whose virility is impaired.
It is aphrodisiac, life-promoting, increases semen, and produces offspring.
Taṇḍulīyaka, bṛhatī, nāgavallī, tagara, and punarnavā,
hilamocikā, maṇḍūkaparṇī, bitter ākhukarṇikā,
madana and arka as well, together with lac, sutamātṛkā, and the milks called sudhā, are prescribed.
Grinding abhraka with plantain and the like and with salt, making it into discs, and placing it within those leaves,
when the fuel has burned, it is perfected by the wind of a fan and by a puṭa of water from the roots of snuhī and arka.

children.text: dhānyābhrakasya bhāgaikaṃ bhāgau dvau ṭaṅkaṇasya ca
children.translated_text: One part of dhānyābhraka and two parts of borax
should be ground, sealed in a blind crucible, and cooked with intense fire.
When naturally cooled, the powder should be used in all formulations.
Dhānyābhraka should be rubbed firmly with the milks of arka for the length of a day.
It should be wrapped in arka leaves and made into a wheel shape.

children.text: kuñjarākhye puṭe dagdhvā saptavārān punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having burned it in the heating called kuñjara seven times again and again,
then in the same way three puṭas should be given with decoctions of banyan roots.
It is killed; there is no doubt here, and it should be used in all formulations.
The three milks, the water of kumārī, gaṅgā leaves, human urine,
banyan sprouts, and goat's blood: with these one should triturate abhraka.
When heated one hundred times, an ash is produced like a ruby.
Vyoma becomes lusterless; in a purified body it is a rasāyana.

children.text: niścandramāritaṃ vyoma rūpaṃ vīryyaṃ dṛḍhaṃ tanum
children.translated_text: Vyoma that has been killed until lusterless makes beauty, potency, and the body firm.
It destroys death and the mass of old age and diseases.
Haritāla is called tālamāla, māla, the ornament of actors,
piñjaka, remover of hair, tālaka, and also pīta, the yellow one.
Tālaka is twofold, leaf-like and lump-like; of these the first is best.
Impure tāla destroys life and causes kapha, vāta, and urinary disorders.
It produces burning, eruptions, and contractions of the limbs; therefore it should be purified.
Tālaka becomes purified when it has been steamed in the water of kūṣmāṇḍa; thereafter,
when washed separately in lime-water and oil, it does not cause harm.

children.text: tālakaṃ kaṇaśaḥ kṛtvā daśāṃśena ca ṭaṅkaṇam
children.translated_text: Having broken tālaka into small particles, with one tenth part of ṭaṅkaṇa,
one should wash it with liquids produced from jambīra, and then wash it again with sour gruel.

children.text: vastre caturguṇe baddhvā dolāyaṃtre dinaṃ pacet
children.translated_text: Having tied it in a fourfold cloth, one should cook it for a day in a dolāyantra.
Having powdered it, it should be steamed for a day with āranāla and with juices born from kūṣmāṇḍa,
or with waters of śālmalī; tālaka thereby obtains purification.

children.text: tālakaṃ poṭṭalīṃ baddhvā sacūrṇe kāṃjike pacet
children.translated_text: Having tied tālaka in a bundle, one should cook it in sour gruel containing powder,
for one yāma by means of a dolāyantra, and then in juice of kūṣmāṇḍa.
One should cook it for a yāma in sesame oil and for a yāma in water of triphalā.
Cooked for four yāmas in a dolāyantra, tālaka is purified.
Having made very pure tālaka into particles inside another pot,
and ground it with lime-water and with substances arising from roots of apāmārga,
and ground it with alkaline waters, one should place above and below it powder produced from barley awns,
seal it, and then fill it with kūṣmāṇḍas.
Having sealed the mouth again, one should cook it for four yāmas with gradually increased fire.
In this way that powder should be cooked, and then employed in kuṣṭha and similar diseases.

children.text: haritālaṃ kaṭu snigdhaṃ kaṣāyaṃ ca visarpanut
children.translated_text: Haritāla is pungent, unctuous, and astringent, and removes visarpa.
Tālaka removes diseases such as kuṣṭha, deathly affliction, and fever.
When well purified, it produces beauty, strength, and vigor, and destroys death.
Likewise, with lemon water and then with lime-water,
having washed it, one should place it in a pit with twice as much śālmalī alkali,
make a kavacī apparatus, and fill it with sand.
After cooking it for twelve praharas and letting it cool by itself, one should powder it.
One should feed a single raktikā of it for the pacification of kuṣṭha and ślīpada.
The tālaka called bamboo-leaf should be placed in water of kūṣmāṇḍa,

children.text: saptadhā vā tridhā vāpi dadhnā cāmlena vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seven times or even three times, and again in curd or in sour liquid.
After purifying it, one should dry it again and powder it to the size of rice grains.
Then the skilled physician should place a shallow dish in a vessel.
The physician should smear it with paste produced from young leaves of badarī.
Fire should be applied until the lower vessel becomes reddish.
When removed after self-cooling, it will surely have the appearance of ruby.
One should eat two raktikās of that, triturated with ghee and honey.
Having worshipped the lord of the gods, one is freed from diseases of kuṣṭha.
It destroys what is cracked, what is suppurating, vātarakta, fistula,
sinus ulcers, wounds, malignant wounds, venereal sores, and vicarcikā,
diseases arising in the nose and mouth, and very severe injuries.

children.text: puṇḍarīkaṃ ca carmākhyaṃ visphoṭaṃ maṇḍalaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: It also destroys puṇḍarīka, the skin disease, blisters, and maṇḍala likewise.
Manaḥśilā is also called naipālī, śilāhvā, and nāgajihvikā.
Manohvā, kunaṭī, goṇī, karañjī, and karavīrikā,
and manohvā, resembling the flower of oṇḍra, are praised for all applications.

children.text: manaḥśilā mandabalaṃ ca nūnaṃ karoti jantoḥ śubhapākahīnā
children.translated_text: Manaḥśilā, when lacking proper processing, certainly makes a creature weak and deficient in good digestion.

children.text: malaṃ tu baddhaṃ kurute ca nūnaṃ saśarkaraṃ kṛcchragadaṃ karoti ||
children.translated_text: It certainly binds the stool and, with gravel, causes the disease of painful urination.
Impure śilā produces stone, urinary disease, and heart disease.
It causes weak digestion and corruption of the stool; purified, it removes all pains.
Śilā, with juices produced from jayantī and bhṛṅgarāja and with juice of red agastya,

children.text: dolāyantrair dinaṃ pācyā yāmaṃ chāgasya mūtrake
children.translated_text: should be cooked for a day in dolāyantras, and for one yāma in goat's urine.
One should wash it with āranāla and employ it in all diseases.
Manaḥśilā ground with juices of mātuluṅga and with water of jayā,
or else with juices of śṛṅgavera, becomes purified.

children.text: kaṭuḥ snigdhā śilā tiktā kaphaghnī lekhanī sarā
children.translated_text: Śilā is pungent, unctuous, bitter, phlegm-destroying, scraping, and mobile.
Auspicious śilā destroys fear from possession by spirits and removes cough and asthma.

children.text: puṣpāṇāṃ raktapītānāṃ rasaiḥ piṣṭvā ca bhāvayet
children.translated_text: Having ground kharpara with juices of red and yellow flowers, one should impregnate it,
with human urine, cow urine, barley-sour gruel, and rock salt,
for seven days or even for three days; afterwards kharpara is purified.
Kharpara, thoroughly heated and immersed seven times,
inside the juice of lemon seeds, attains freedom from impurity.
One should cook kharpara together with mercury in a sand apparatus.
Having powdered it for as long as a day, a fine ash is produced.
Kharpara is heavy, moistening, removes urinary diseases, and destroys wasting disease.
For tuttha, there are the names śikhigrīva, hemasāra, and mayūraka.
One should triturate tuttha with the dung of a cat and a pigeon.

children.text: daśāṃśaṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ dattvā pācyaṃ mṛdupuṭe tataḥ
children.translated_text: Having added one tenth part of ṭaṅkaṇa, it should then be cooked in a mild puṭa.
For the purification of tuttha, they say, a puṭa should be given with salt and honey.
Tuttha equal to camel dung, with honey and with a quarter part of ṭaṅkaṇa added,
well heated three times by puṭa, is purified and free from vomiting and dizziness.
Tuttha together with an equal amount of sulphur, and half of half the amount of tuttha,

children.text: vāntibhrāntī yadā na stastadā siddhiṃ vinirdiśet ||
children.translated_text: when vomiting and dizziness are absent, then one should declare success.
Tuttha is pungent, alkaline, astringent, clear, and light.
It is scraping, purgative, beneficial to the eyes, and removes itching, worms, and poison.
In urine, āranāla, oils, cow's milk, and plantain juice,
in horse-gram and kodrava decoctions, mākṣika and vimala likewise,
should repeatedly be steamed, placed in elephant-foot yam tuber, with excellent fire.
Together with alkalis, acids, and salts, and mixed with oil and ghee,
three puṭas should be given; after that it becomes purified.
For the purification of vimala, it should be steamed with the juices of jambīra
and likewise with the juices of meṣaśṛṅgī, or cooked for a day with plantain water.
Mākṣika, dhātumākṣika, heated and born from the Tāpī river,

children.text: garuḍo mākṣikaḥ pakṣī bṛhadvarṇa iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: garuḍa, mākṣika, pakṣin, and bṛhadvarṇa: these are remembered as its names.
When broken it resembles gold, while externally it has a slightly black luster.

children.text: bṛhadvarṇa iti khyāto mākṣikaḥ śreṣṭha ucyate ||
children.translated_text: This mākṣika, known as bṛhadvarṇa, is said to be the best.
Impure mākṣika causes weak digestion, loss of strength, wounds, constipation, and pain in the limbs;
it causes death. There is no doubt about this.
One should bind powdered svarṇamākṣika in a cloth and cook it
by the dolā method in a decoction of kālamāriṣa and śāli.
What has fallen down from it is excellent; in this way mākṣika is purified.

children.text: mākṣikasya trayo bhāgā bhāgaikaṃ saindhavasya ca
children.translated_text: Three parts of mākṣika and one part of saindhava salt
should be cooked with the liquid of mātuluṅga, or else with liquid produced from jambīra.
One should cook it in an iron vessel and stir it with an iron ladle
until it becomes bright in color; then mākṣika is purified.
Having added sulphur equal to one quarter of the mākṣika, one should triturate it
with the oil of urubūka, and then make it into small discs.
After placing it in a sealed pair of earthen saucers, one should heat it with a gajapuṭa.
The ash of mākṣika becomes like vermilion; there is no doubt.
Mākṣika is bitter and sweet, removes urinary disease, piles, worms, and skin disease,
alleviates kapha and pitta, is strengthening, a yogavāhin, and a rasāyana.
Kāśīśa is called dhātukāśīśa, khecara, and dantarañjana.
Kāśīśa steamed once with the water of bhṛṅga becomes pure.
Pure kāśīśa is smooth and removes leucoderma and eye disease.
It pacifies bilious epilepsy and, like rasa, produces beneficial qualities.
Rājapaṭṭa, mahāpaṭṭa, śikhigrīva, and virāṭaka are its names.
Powdered kāntapāṣāṇa, mixed with buffalo milk,
should be cooked carefully in an iron vessel with cow ghee.

children.text: lavaṇe ca tathā kṣāre śobhāñjanarase kṣipet
children.translated_text: One should place it in salt, likewise in alkali, and in the juice of śobhāñjana,
and expose it to the sun for a day with water from the sour group.
In the same way, a wise person should cook it twice in the dolikā apparatus.
When the kāntapāṣāṇa has been purified, one may undertake operations with mercury.
Varāṭikā is yellowish, knotty on the back, and has a long stalk.
The best weighs one and a half niṣkas; the middling one weighs a niṣka.
The inferior is said to weigh three quarters of a niṣka.
That is designated by rasa physicians with the name varāṭaka.
Varāṭī should be steamed in sour gruel until it obtains purity.
It destroys pain from indigestion and the like, removes wasting, and cures grahaṇī disorder.
It is pungent, hot, digestive, aphrodisiac, bitter, and removes vāta and kapha.

children.text: bhūgartte ca same śuddhe pattanaṃ sthāpayet sudhīḥ
children.translated_text: In an even and clean pit in the earth, a wise physician should place a vessel
and fill its middle somewhat with husk.
In the middle of it he should place a crucible filled with varāṭa.
Then he should apply a cow-dung fire; this is the excellent pālikā apparatus.
By this, varāṭa is certainly killed and becomes a conqueror of all diseases.
Having powdered nīlāñjana and impregnated it with jambīra liquid,

children.text: dinaikam ātape śuddhaṃ tataḥ kāryeṣu yojayet ||
children.translated_text: it is purified after one day in the sun; then it should be used in operations.
Hiṅgula is called hiṅgulu, darada, and śukatuṇḍaka.
Hiṅgula, arising from mercury and sulphur, is also called daityaraktaka.
Darada, ground with liquids of the sour group and with buffalo
milk seven times, becomes purified when it has dried.
Darada impregnated with ewe's milk and with sour liquids
seven times, carefully, certainly attains purification.
Darada cooked in the dolikā apparatus with liquids born from jambīra,
and impregnated seven times with goat urine, becomes purified.
If hiṅgula is impregnated seven times with fresh ginger and lakuca liquids,

children.text: hiṃgulaḥ śuddhatāṃ yāti nirdoṣo jāyate khalu ||
children.translated_text: it attains purity and indeed becomes free from defects.
Divine hiṅgula is like bimbī fruit and arises from mercury and sulphur.
It removes urinary disease and skin disease, is palatable, strengthening, and increases intelligence and digestive fire.
Śilājatu is called śaileya, adrya, girija, aśmaja,
dhātuja, aśmajatuka, śailaja, and aśmasambhava.
Śilājatu ground with cow milk, triphalā, and liquids of bhṛṅga,
for one day in an iron vessel certainly attains purification.
Śilājatu is bitter and pungent, and is a rasāyana.
It destroys wasting, swelling, abdominal disease, and piles, and conquers pain of the bladder.

children.text: sauvīraṃ ṭaṅkaṇaṃ śaṅkhaṃ kaṃkuṣṭhaṃ gairikaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Sauvīra, ṭaṅkaṇa, śaṅkha, kaṃkuṣṭha, and gairika
should be purified like varāṭa and become free from defects.

children.text: kaṃkuṣṭhaṃ gairikaṃ śaṃkhaṃ kāśīśaṃ ṭaṅgaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Kaṃkuṣṭha, gairika, śaṅkha, kāśīśa, ṭaṅgaṇa,
nīlāñjana, the varieties of oyster shell, small copper substances, and varāṭaka,
steamed with jambīra water and washed with warm water,
attain purity; these should be used by physicians for the success of formulations.
Ṭaṅkaṇa is krāmaṇa, ṣṭaṅga, proper alkali, and digestive.
It is subhaga, born of mālatī, liquefying, and gives purification to iron.
First, having taken ṭaṅkaṇa, one should place it in sour kāñjika.
After one night, having taken it out, one should expose it in the solar apparatus.
The ṭaṅga should be placed in human urine and likewise in cow urine.
At the end of the day, having taken it out from that, it should then be placed in jambīra water.
After taking it out from the sour liquid of jambīra, it should be placed in a coconut vessel.
Mixed with powdered pepper, one should wash it with cold water.
Taking <s>ṭaṅka</s> (borax) in this way, one should employ it in all diseases.
<s>Ṭaṃkaṇa</s> is fire-kindling, dry, kapha-destroying, purgative, and light.
A skilled man should take one pala of conch placed in a blind crucible,
mix it with half a māṣa of <s>ṭaṅkaṇa</s>, and kill it by means of the daṇḍa apparatus.
Conch destroys all pains, especially abdominal disease;
it removes colic, sour pitta, constipation, and urinary disorders, and kindles the digestive fire.
Hear the purification and killing of metals beginning with gold and ending with iron-rust.

children.text: taile takre gavāṃ mūtre kāñjike'tha kulatthaje ||
children.translated_text: In oil, buttermilk, cow urine, sour gruel, and then in the decoction of horse-gram,
one should sprinkle the metals, heated very hot, seven times in each respective liquid.
In this way the metals beginning with gold attain purity, without doubt.

children.text: saukhyaṃ vīryyaṃ balaṃ hanti nānārogaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: Impure nectar-like gold destroys happiness, potency, and strength, and produces many diseases;
therefore, once purified, gold should be killed.
Having been impregnated for five days with earth and the sour juice of citron,
one should purify it with earth, ash, and half a measure of salt, and then give it a puṭa-heating.
Anthill earth, soot, red ochre, brick, and salt:
these are the five earths; having ground them with citron juice and sour gruel,

children.text: piṣṭvā lepyaṃ svarṇapatraṃ puṭena tu viśudhyati
children.translated_text: gold leaf smeared with them is purified by a puṭa-heating.
One should keep the five earths on gold leaves for three days.
Mākṣika and lead powder, ground with the juice of arka,
kill gold leaf by a puṭa-heating in a mere moment.
Having added well-purified mercury, one should carefully make a base-cake.
After placing lead powder above and below, it is surely killed by a puṭa-heating.
To molten gold one should add lead in a sixteenth part,
then take it out and triturate it with lemon water.
Having made a ball, one should place an equal amount of sulfur powder over it.
Having put it in a covered pair of earthen dishes, one should heat it with thirty forest cow-dung cakes.
In this way, by sage-puṭas, gold does not regain its metallic state again.

children.text: śuddhasūtasamaṃ svarṇaṃ khalle kṛtvā tu golakam
children.translated_text: Placing gold equal to purified mercury in a mortar, one should make a ball.

children.text: ūrdhvādho gandhakaṃ dattvā sarvatulyaṃ nirudhya ca ||
children.translated_text: After putting sulfur above and below, equal to the whole, and sealing it,
one should give puṭa-heatings with thirty forest cow-dung cakes; in this way, fourteen times.

children.text: nirutthaṃ jāyate bhasma gandho deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: A non-revivable ash is produced; sulfur should be supplied again and again.
Gold is astringent, bitter, and sweet; it is heavy and scraping.

children.text: hṛdyaṃ rasāyanaṃ balyaṃ cakṣuṣyaṃ kāntidaṃ śuci ||
children.translated_text: It is good for the heart, a rasāyana, strengthening, beneficial to the eyes, beauty-giving, and pure.
It gives life, intelligence, steadiness of age, purity of speech, and memory.
It is the supreme destroyer of wasting disease, insanity groups, and skin diseases.
That which, after being burned, passes the test, is very cool, spotless, and like jasmine,
heavy, unctuous, and soft: that is considered the best silver.

children.text: āyuḥ śukraṃ balaṃ hanti rogasaṃghaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: Impure and killed silver destroys life, semen, and strength, and causes a mass of diseases;

children.text: aśuddhaṃ ca mṛtaṃ tāraṃ śuddhaṃ māryamato budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore the wise should kill it after it has been purified.
Silver melted with lead and the king of alkalis attains purity,
or, freed from faults, it may be cooked with alkali and acid.
Mākṣika and sulfur should likewise be triturated with the milk of arka.

children.text: tena liptaṃ rūpyapatraṃ puṭena mriyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: Silver leaf smeared with that is surely killed by a puṭa-heating.
After placing double the amount of hiṅgula on silver leaf pierced at the edge,
mercury should be collected in a distillation apparatus; the silver is said to be killed.
One should grind orpiment, sulfur, and silver leaf with liquids of lemon and similar fruits.
With three puṭa-heatings it becomes ash; this should be used in mercurial and other preparations.
Four parts of silver leaf and one part of purified orpiment
should be ground with liquids produced from citron, and the silver leaves should be smeared.
After sealing, it should be cooked with three puṭas using twenty-five forest cow-dung cakes.

children.text: mriyate nātra sandeho gandho deyaḥ punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It is killed, there is no doubt here; sulfur should be supplied again and again.
Silver is cold, astringent, sweet, and sour; it conquers aggravation of vāta.
It kindles digestion, produces strength, is unctuous, and destroys abdominal tumors and indigestion.
Silver is remembered as life-promoting, destroyer of chronic disease, and scraping.
They do not call poison poison; copper is called poison.

children.text: eko doṣo viṣe tvaṣṭau doṣāstāmre prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is one fault in poison, but eight faults are declared in copper.
Dizziness, fainting, burning, nausea, emaciation, and vomiting,
loss of taste and mental distress: these faults are like poison.
Therefore only thoroughly purified copper should be taken for the pacification of disease.
One should smear copper leaves with salt and the milk of arka.
Heating them in fire, one should sprinkle them again and again in juice of nirguṇḍī.
One should cook the copper leaf for a yāma in cow urine over a strong fire.

children.text: śudhyate nātra sandeho māraṇaṃ cātra kathyate ||
children.translated_text: It is purified, there is no doubt here; its killing is now explained.

children.text: sūtamekaṃ dvidhā gandhaṃ yāmaṃ mardyaṃ tu kanyayā
children.translated_text: One part mercury and two parts sulfur should be triturated for a yāma with kumārī.
Smearing copper leaf equal to both with it, one should place it in a pot.

children.text: samyak śūraṇajaiḥ sārddhaṃ pārśve bhasma nidhāpayet
children.translated_text: Together with material produced from śūraṇa, one should properly place ash at the side.
One should cook it for four yāmas on a hearth, with cow dung on the back of the vessel.
Water should be added again and again; when naturally cooled, one should triturate it.
It is killed, there is no doubt here; one should use it in all diseases.
Place copper leaf together with sulfur in water of jambīra mixed with rock salt.

children.text: pakvāyamānaṃ puṭayetsuyuktvā vāntyādikaṃ yāvad upaiti śāntim ||
children.translated_text: While it is being cooked, one should give a well-arranged puṭa-heating until vomiting and the other disorders come to rest.

children.text: śuddhaṃ tāmradalaṃ vimardya paṭunā kṣāreṇa jambīrajair nīrair ghasram idaṃ snugarkapayasā liptaṃ dhametsaptadhā
children.translated_text: Having triturated purified copper leaf with salt, alkali, and waters produced from citron, one should smear it for a day with the milks of snuhī and arka and blow it in the furnace seven times.

children.text: nirguṇḍyambu himaṃ rasendrakalitaṃ dugdhājyagandhena tattulyenātha mṛtaṃ bhavetsupuṭitaṃ pañcāmṛtena tridhā ||
children.translated_text: Water of nirguṇḍī, cooled, mixed with rasendra, with the scent of milk and ghee equal to it, then becomes dead when well heated three times with pañcāmṛta.

children.text: vāntibhrāntivivarjitaṃ jayarujā kuṣṭhāni pāṇḍvāmayaṃ śūlaṃ mehagudāṅkurānilagadān uktānupānair jayet
children.translated_text: Free from vomiting and dizziness, it conquers jaya-disease, skin diseases, anemia, colic, urinary disease, hemorrhoidal growths, and disorders of vāta, with the stated vehicles.

children.text: guñjāmātram idaṃ tato dviguṇitaṃ tacchuddhakāyena ced bhuktaṃ sthaulyajarāpamṛtyuśamanaṃ pathyāśinā vatsarāt ||
children.translated_text: If this is eaten in a dose of one guñjā, and then twice that, by one whose body is purified and who eats wholesome food, within a year it calms corpulence, old age, and untimely death.
Copper is hot, removes poison, and takes away diseases of the liver, spleen, and abdomen.
It destroys worms, colic, āma-vāta, and conquers grahaṇī disease, hemorrhoids, and acid pitta.
Lead and tin, when melted, should be quenched with the milk of arka.
After three times, they have come to purification inside a perforated pot.
Tin, boiled in water mixed with powder, is purified in half a yāma.

children.text: bhujaṅgamam agastyaṃ ca piṣṭvā patraṃ pralepayet
children.translated_text: Having ground bhujaṅgama and agastya, one should smear the leaf.
There, when the lead is completely melted, the alkali produced from vāsā and apāmārga
should be mixed into it, one quarter part according to the teacher's instruction.
One should cook it on the hearth for a watch, and stir it with a ladle of vāsā wood.
Then, having taken out that powder, one should triturate it with the juice of vāsā.

children.text: evaṃ saptapuṭair nāgaṃ sindūraṃ jāyate dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: In this way, through seven puṭa-heatings, lead certainly becomes sindūra.
Lead, triturated with vāsā juice, through three kumbhī-puṭas,
together with śilā, becomes ash; that powder conquers every urinary disorder.
Killed lead bears the strength of ten elephants and increases virility, life span, and complexion.

children.text: mehānhanti hataṃ nāgaṃ sevyaṃ vaṅgaṃ ca tadguṇam ||
children.translated_text: It destroys urinary disorders; tin too should be used, having the same qualities.
Lead is the colorant of silver; it removes vāta, pitta, and kapha.
It removes grahaṇī disease, skin disease, abdominal tumors, hemorrhoids, consumption, wounds, and poison.
Tin, together with tāla and arka, should be ground with milk and sealed in a covered vessel.
With bark produced from dried aśvattha, one should bring it to the state of ash seven times.
The purified leaves of tin should be melted inside a pot.
Powder produced from apāmārga, equal in amount to it, should be mixed there.
With a large-tipped iron ladle one should slowly rub it down.
Until it attains the state of ash, it should be rubbed as before.
Then the physician should make the powder into one mass, free from charcoal,
and seal it with a new saucer.
Afterwards, cooked with intense fire, it certainly becomes tin-bhasma.
The wise man should put tin in a kharpara vessel and set it on the hearth.
When it has become liquid, he should then add these powders to it.
First, powder of rajanī; second, yāmānikā;
third, cumin, and then what is produced from tamarind bark.
He should also place there powder arising from aśvattha bark.

children.text: evaṃ vidhānato vaṅgaṃ mriyate nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: By this method tin is killed; there is no doubt here.
Tin is bitter and sour, dry, and somewhat aggravating to vāta.
It destroys diseases of fat and phlegm, kills worms, and removes urinary disease.
All metals, heated and then plunged into water from plantain root,
seven times, attain unsurpassed purification.
In water eight times the quantity of triphalā, with sixteen palas of triphalā,
in that decoction, reduced to one quarter, five palas of iron
should be made into heated plates and quenched seven times.
In this way the fault born from iron in the mountain-born metal is dissolved.
By sun-cooking, by pot-cooking, and by puṭa-cooking,
iron becomes non-revivable and gives the results that have been stated.

children.text: lauhe dṛṣadi lauhaṃ ca mudgareṇa hataṃ muhuḥ
children.translated_text: Iron on an iron stone, struck repeatedly with a hammer,
should be made to pass through water and purified with water or with triphalā water.
Afterwards one should wash it many times and keep each other substance separate.
Dried by the rays of the sun, it should be used for sun-cooking.
For washing and sun-cooking, triphalā equal to the iron is used.
Having added twice as much water, it is reduced until one fourth remains.
Having repeatedly added this stated water of fruit decoction,
one should dry it continually for three days by the heat of the sun.

children.text: athavā tatra tatkvāthaṃ dattvā dattvā bhiṣagvaraḥ
children.translated_text: Or, there the excellent physician, adding that decoction again and again,
should purify it seven times, each with sevenfold sets.
Thus, at the end of sun-cooking, he should carry out cooking in a pot.
In pot-cooking, the fruit should be taken at three times the iron.
Water sixteen times that amount is reduced until one eighth remains.
For soft, medium, and hard irons, and for the others, the measure is equal to the iron.
Taking what is to be decocted, four, eight, and sixteen
times as much water is set down and reduced until it equals the iron.
In pot-cooking, fresh juice too is equal in relation to the iron.
Having placed the decoction and the rest in the pot, prepared according to rule,

children.text: pākena kṣīyate yasmāt sthālīpāka iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: because it is reduced by cooking, it is remembered as pot-cooking.
The root of hastikarṇapalāśa and śatamūlikā,
together with the natural juices of these plants called bhṛṅgarāja and rājā,
may be mixed in, or should be used in pot-cooking after the fruit and the rest.
Pot-cooking may also be performed with a medicine appropriate to the doṣa.
When it has been well cooked in pot-cooking, it should be washed with clear water.
Dried and carefully powdered, it should be used in puṭa-cooking.
From the puṭa comes the destruction of faults; from the puṭa alone arises excellence.
And from the puṭa iron is killed; therefore one should perform the puṭa-heating.

children.text: yathā yathā pradīyante puṭāḥ subahuśo yadi
children.translated_text: In whatever way puṭas are applied, if they are very numerous,
In this way and that, they produce thousands of qualities.
But what has been cooked by puṭa-heating is praised in operations with rasa.
For disease, the method of puṭas is considered to range from ten up to one hundred.
For rasāyana, a puṭa should be given from one hundred up to one thousand.
In aphrodisiac treatment it should be known as ranging from ten to five hundred.
One should puṭa-heat the metal only until, when powdered in water,
it rises up lightly in still water like a swan.
For the medicine used in puṭa-heating too, either a decoction or fresh juice
should be prepared by the best physicians according to the measure to be stated.

children.text: rasābhāve tu sarveṣāṃ kvātho grāhyo manīṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: When fresh juice is lacking in all cases, the wise should take a decoction.
And even when the fresh juice is absent, a decoction from the triphalā and other drugs is used.
Triphalā, trivṛt, dantī, kaṭukī, tālamūlikā,
vṛddhadāru, vṛścīra, vṛṣapatraka, and citraka,
śṛṅgavera and viḍaṅga, bhṛṅga and bhallātaka as the drug,
pomegranate leaves, śatapatrī, and punarnavā,
kuṭhāraka and krāmaka, the tuber tantrī, bhekasya parṇikā,
hastikarṇa, palāśa, kuliśa, and keśarājaka,
māṇa, khaṇḍitakarṇa, gojihvā, and lohamāraka,
and giriśāntanaka are named; this is the triphalā group.
The learned prescribe these for general puṭa-heating.
For special puṭa-heating, hear the other groups that are taught.

children.text: eraṇḍaḥ śārivā drākṣā śirīṣaṃ ca prasāriṇī ||
children.translated_text: Eraṇḍa, śārivā, drākṣā, śirīṣa, and prasāriṇī,
the two leafy plants called māṣa and mudga, vidārīkanda, and ketakī:
this is the eraṇḍa group, removing all disorders of vāta.
Kirāta, amṛtā, nimba, kustumburu, and śatāvarī,
paṭola, candana, padma, śālmalī, uḍumbarī, and jaṭā:
this kirāta group is regarded as destroying pitta disorders.
Roots of śṛṅgavera, nirguṇḍī, kauṭaja fruit,
the two karañjas, mūrvā, śobhāñjana, and śirīṣaka,
varuṇa, arka leaves, paṭola, and kaṇṭakārikā:
this śṛṅgavera group removes diseases of śleṣman.
Gokṣura and kṣuraka, vyāghrī, the two siṃhapucchīs, and sthirā:
this is called the gokṣura group, removing vāta and śleṣman.
Paṭola leaves, uśīra, kāsamarda, and aparājitā,
lodhra, indīvara, kahlāra, vārāhī, together with kāntā:
this should be known as the paṭola group, removing diseases of pitta and śleṣman.
Kiṃśuka, kāśmarī, viśva, agnimantha, and trikaṇṭaka,
śyonāka, śālaparṇī, the two siṃhapucchīs, and sthirā,

children.text: pāṭalā kaṇṭakārī ca bṛhatī bilva eva ca
children.translated_text: pāṭalā, kaṇṭakārī, bṛhatī, and bilva:
this kiṃśuka group is regarded as removing the three doṣas.
Śatāvarī, balā, dhātrī, guḍūcī, and vṛddhadāraka,
vānarī, the plant called bhṛṅgarāja, vidārī, gokṣura, and kṣura,
joined with vājigandhā and kaṇā, is praised in aphrodisiac treatments.
With vidārīkanda, piṇḍāhva, bhṛṅgarāja, śatāvarī,
muṇḍirī, and keśarāja, a puṭa should be given in rasāyana.

children.text: sāmānye ca viśeṣe ca puṭe yadyatprakīrtitam
children.translated_text: Whatever has been mentioned for the general and special puṭa,
with those, mixed together or one by one as desired, one should then perform puṭa-heating.
In puṭa-heating, the taking of fruits and the like should be equal in measure to the iron.
In a pit measuring one hasta, half-filled with cow-dung fuel,
or half-filled with husk and wood, one should place it.
Then, having put the iron into the fire, one should fill above it in the same way.

children.text: divā vā yadi vā rātrau vidhinānena pācayet
children.translated_text: Whether by day or by night, one should cook it by this procedure.
By puṭa-heating for just four praharas, one should kill it.

children.text: puṭapāke kṣaṇād ūrdhvaṃ sthito bhavati bhasmasāt
children.translated_text: In puṭa-heating, if it remains for more than a moment, it becomes reduced to ash.
But if it is drawn out from below, it becomes weak in potency.
When it is in the pit, covered with ash and very cold, it should be drawn out.
If it is drawn out while hot, loss of its qualities arises.
One part of purified king mercury and two parts of bali
should be triturated with an equal amount of iron powder from the two, using the liquids of kanyā.
Then, after two yāmas, one should make a ball and place it in a copper vessel.
Covering it with leaves of eraṇḍa, it should become heated after two yāmas.
Kept for three nights in a heap of grain, one should then triturate it firmly.
That powder, strained through cloth, floats on water like a swan.

children.text: tīkṣṇaṃ muṇḍaṃ kāntalauhaṃ nirutthaṃ jāyate mṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Tīkṣṇa, muṇḍa, and kānta iron become dead and niruttha.
Or one should add darada in a twelfth part to the powder of tīkṣṇa iron.
Having triturated it with kanyā water for two yāmas, one should enclose it.
Thus, with seven puṭas, the iron powder attains death.
All this dead iron should be cooked with the five mitras.
If it is thus niruttha, four raktis should be used.
Honey, ghee, guñjā, ṭaṅgaṇa, and guggulu:
this is counted as the mitrapañcaka in the union of metals.
Cow ghee, sulfur, and iron should be triturated in a heated mortar.
For one day with kanyā liquids; having sealed it, one should cook it in a gajapuṭa.
In this way all irons should be made niruttha.
One should also triturate iron ash with guñjā, honey, ghee, and ṭaṅgaṇa.
One should blow it in the fire; then the iron is fit to be applied in rasāyana.
Black iron removes swelling, pain, piles, worms, pallor, and wasting.
It is age-sustaining, heavy, beneficial to the eyes, and removes all fat and vāta.
It gives life, produces strength and virility, removes disease, and acts as an aphrodisiac.

children.text: ayaḥsamānaṃ nahi kiṃcid asti rasāyanaṃ śreṣṭhatamaṃ narāṇām ||
children.translated_text: There is no <s>rasāyana</s> (rejuvenating elixir) for men better than iron.

children.text: kūṣmāṇḍaṃ tilatailaṃ ca rasonaṃ rājikāṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Kūṣmāṇḍa, sesame oil, garlic, and likewise mustard,
liquor and sour tastes too: one who uses iron should avoid these.
Krauñca is twice as good as the ordinary kind; kāliṅga is eight times better than that.
Bhadra is a hundred times better than kali, and vajra is a thousand times better than bhadra.
Pāṇḍi is a hundred times better than vajra; niraṅga is ten times better,
and beyond that, by thousands of crores, kāntalauha is greatly efficacious.

children.text: ye guṇā mārite muṇḍe te guṇā muṇḍakiṭṭake
children.translated_text: The qualities that exist in killed muṇḍa iron are the qualities in muṇḍa slag.
Therefore everywhere one should apply maṇḍūra for the pacification of disease.
Slag more than a hundred years old is best; that eighty years old is middling.
That sixty years old is inferior; anything less than that is like poison.

children.text: dagdhvākṣakāṣṭhair malam āyasaṃ tu gomūtranirvāpitam aṣṭavārān
children.translated_text: Having burned iron slag with akṣa wood and quenched it eight times in cow urine,

children.text: vicūrṇya līḍhaṃ madhunācireṇa kumbhāhvayaṃ pāṇḍugadaṃ nihanti ||
children.translated_text: one should powder it and lick it with honey; it quickly destroys the disease called kumbha and pāṇḍu disease.
Muṇḍa iron is ten times better than slag; tīkṣṇa is more than a hundred times better than muṇḍa.
Kānta is a hundred thousand times better than tīkṣṇa and produces benefit when eaten.

children.text: nāgaiḥ suvarṇaṃ rajataṃ ca tāpyair gandhena tāmraṃ śilayā ca nāgam
children.translated_text: Gold and silver are destroyed by lead and by tāpya; copper by sulphur, and lead by śilā.

children.text: tālena vaṅgaṃ vividhaṃ ca lauhaṃ nārīpayo hanti ca hiṅgulena ||
children.translated_text: Tin and various kinds of iron are destroyed by tāla, and also by women's milk with hiṅgula.
One should steam them in a dolikā apparatus with the fresh juice of jayantī.
Gems, pearls, and corals should be purified in a single watch of time.
Having ground purified pearls in a mortar, one should give them a light puṭa heating.
Thus, through combination with sour gruel, even diamond attains the state of ash.
One should quench them with equal amounts of kumārī and taṇḍulīya,
each seven times, heating them thoroughly again and again.
Pearls, corals, and all gems without exception
are killed in an instant, taking on various colors; there is no doubt here.

children.text: strīdugdhena pravālaṃ ca bhāvayitvā tu haṇḍike
children.translated_text: Having impregnated coral with women's milk in a pot,
one should place it in the middle together with buttermilk and seal that vessel.
On the hearth, by the heat of fire, it is killed in two praharas.
One should cook one hundred palas of kulattha with one droṇa of water.
When one quarter remains, in that decoction eight gems or stones

children.text: ātape tridinaṃ śodhyāḥ kvāthasiktāḥ punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: should be purified for three days in the sun, repeatedly sprinkled with the decoction.
All gems and jewels are purified; there is no doubt.
Having made it the size of a chickpea, one should impregnate it with cow urine for three days.
Ground together with an equal amount of ṭaṅkaṇa, the poison is said to be dead.

children.text: athavā traiphale kvāthe viṣaṃ śudhyati pācitam
children.translated_text: Or poison is purified when cooked in a decoction of triphalā,
cooked in a swing apparatus in triphalā decoction and goat's milk.
One should cook poison in a dolā apparatus in a vessel filled with cow urine,
in an initial measure of ten tolakas, by day and night, O physician.
Having made the portions of poison coarse like chickpeas in a vessel,
one should put cow urine there, fresh each day, constantly.
After three days, one should dry it by keeping it in intense sunlight.
Then one should use that kind in preparations according to the required measure.
Arka, sehuṇḍa, dhustūra, lāṅgalī, karavīra,
guñjā, and ahiphena: these are the seven classes of subsidiary poisons.

children.text: dhustūrasya ca yad bījam anyaccopaviṣaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: The seed of dhustūra, and whatever other subsidiary poison there is,
should be purified in a dolikā apparatus, in a vessel filled with milk.

children.text: nistuṣaṃ jayapālaṃ ca dvidhā kṛtvā vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: The skilled man should take jayapāla with the husk removed and split it in two.
He should remove the middle part of this seed like a leaf.
He should mix it with powder of ṭaṅkaṇa, one eighth in amount.

children.text: keśayantre ca tadbhāvyaṃ pācyaṃ dugdhena saṃplutam
children.translated_text: Then it should be impregnated in a hair-apparatus and cooked, flooded with milk.
In three nights jayapāla attains purification and becomes like nectar.
In one karṣa of tamarind-leaf juice, filtered through cloth, two palas
of snuhī latex should be carefully impregnated in a raudra apparatus by the wise man.
When the liquid has dried, he should take it out and use it in all preparations.
One should keep an old leech in copper vessels.
For four months one should put niśā powder into eight palas of water.

children.text: tasminkṣipet jalaukāṃ tāṃ svayaṃ lālāṃ parityajet
children.translated_text: Into that one should put that leech; it will itself give up its saliva.

children.text: tyaktalālā jalaukā ca sā yojyā raktamokṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: A leech that has given up its saliva is fit to be used for bloodletting.

children.text: romapṛṣṭhā ca kapilā raktarekhā ca durbalā
children.translated_text: One with a hairy back, tawny, with red lines, or weak
should especially be avoided by a physician who desires fame.
First taking the seed, the wise man should dry it in a raudra apparatus
carefully with a liquid slightly mixed with rock salt,
or with water of apāmārga: this is the purification of vārdhakya seed.
One pala of vṛddhadāraka seed should be cooked in dolā fashion
in vessels filled with milk; then it is certainly purified.
One should purify nimbu seed with apāmārga decoction.
The purification of jayapāla seed is with root decoctions and kumārī.
The seed of rājavṛkṣa is purified with decoctions of indravāruṇikā.
The purification of dhustūra seed is with uttaravāruṇī together with its root.
Śigru seeds, cotton seeds, and apāmārga seed:

children.text: gharmeṇa śodhanaṃ teṣāṃ na dadyātsaindhavaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: their purification is by heat; after that one should not add rock salt.
Bitter koṣātakī, dantī, paṭolī, and indravāruṇī,
kaṭutumbī, devadālī, and kākatuṇḍī are purified.
Mahākāla is purified only with the juice of dhātrī fruit.
The seeds of the two kinds of karañja should be purified with bhṛṅgarāja.
All seeds beginning with <s>gunja</s> are to be purified with human urine, without alkaline salt.
The fruit produced from <s>bhallataka</s> is to be purified with coconut water.
Especially in a decoction of <s>guduci</s> and <s>triphala</s>, and also in milk,

children.text: paktvā ca khaṇḍaśaḥ śuddhaṃ gṛhṇīyānmṛdu guggulum ||
children.translated_text: having cooked it in pieces, one should take the soft <s>guggulu</s> when purified.
